target: क्या तुम्हें पता है कि अगली मीटिंग कब है?
english: Do you know when the next meeting is?
reason: UNNATURAL/translationese: "क्या तुम यह जानते हो कि..." is a word-for-word rendering of English "Do you know that..."; spoken Hindi uses पता है, and the dummy यह makes it stilted. Same embedded कि-clause question is kept.

target: हमारे परिवार में छह लोग हैं।
english: There are six people in our family.
reason: Textbook motto: "three generations live together in our house" is a culture-lesson set piece a learner will never say. Replaced with the same number + में + हैं pattern in a sentence learners actually use when introducing their family.

target: मेरे पिताजी एक स्कूल में टीचर हैं।
english: My father is a teacher at a school.
reason: Boastful textbook filler ("a successful businessman") – the सफल adds status-signalling nobody says in ordinary talk. Keeps the same एक + noun + हैं frame with an everyday occupation.

target: डेंटिस्ट ने मेरा दाँत भर दिया।
reason: UNNATURAL: "दाँत में भर दिया" leaves भरना without an object – it reads as "filled (something) into the tooth" and no native would phrase it that way. Fixed to the normal ने + perfective compound verb.

target: नमस्ते! आज नाश्ते में क्या बनाया?
english: Hello! What did you make for breakfast today?
reason: Register mismatch: सुप्रभात is formal written/Sanskritised Hindi that clashes with the casual breakfast question; speakers say नमस्ते (or "good morning"). Same greeting + past-tense question structure.
